findings: Both captures document the Files API 45-second server cutoff and an upload from faster infrastructure as a timeout mitigation. Sandbox approval does not itself enroll live mode: resubmit, using the exact same APK for automatic approval. Separate Stripe admin settings deep-link access for a third-party default app from production Android Settings, which Stripe blocks. DevKit language can be changed through Android Settings via adb. The November Build guide says the root Stripe All settings URI always requires the admin PIN. Navigating to it leaves authorization in place.

On compatible readers the integrator must implement app switching. The deploy-time default kiosk app launches during update checks and after payments. Dashboard does not configure multiple apps. Web app packaging uses an Android APK and an SDK JavaScript bridge when using local SDK commands; Stripe's server-driven payments path avoids the bridge and handoff client. The separate November Build guide documents preferred kiosk selection in the Dashboard sandbox DevKit deploy-group workflow.

A production reader restarts the configured default merchant app after a crash and can enter a loop if initialization keeps failing. On a DevKit with the Stripe payment app configured as default it is that app that restarts if the merchant app crashes. The guide's 500 KB IPC state-saving limit makes memory a possible cause when many line items are involved. External persistence is a mitigation. Production logs are not exposed and Stripe points to Sentry.

For a sideloaded DevKit POS to launch after a completed payment, set the preferred kiosk app through a deploy group that includes the DevKit. Upload an app targeting only DevKit types to skip review, then deploy that app version to the group. A deployed production bug is handled by uploading and deploying a corrected new version.
substantive_changes: November broadens the guide's multi-app statement from the named S700/S710 hardware (May) to Apps on Devices-compatible Terminal readers. It retains in-app switching, no launcher, the default kiosk app, the update/payment triggers and no Dashboard multi-app configuration. This is documentation scope, not a proved rollout or exhaustive supported-reader list.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Preserve the May 1 capture and its S700/S710-specific scope despite the filename suffix. Preserve Files API vs other upload paths, approval environments, Stripe admin vs Android Settings, production vs DevKit default-app settings, and DevKit-only review bypass.
November changes issue bullets to headings, adjusts code indentation/numbering, and changes deploy-with-API URL casing. Deployment and kiosk behaviors described in the body are unchanged.
conflicts: The current source's 'Multiple apps on S700/S710' follows the May raw and omits the broader November reader condition. Update it with the Apps on Devices-compatibility qualifier instead of presuming support on all Terminal hardware.

The summary's timeout phrasing loses Files API scope, and its production initialization crash wording turns a possible crash loop into an unqualified outcome. The 500 KB figure is scoped to saving activity state and does not guarantee the crash diagnosis. The separate overview's larger private-preview upload path does not establish a timeout for that path.

The mapped summary's broad Dashboard prohibition should scope to multi-app configuration on a device. It should not read as a ban on preferred kiosk selection in the documented Dashboard DevKit deploy-group workflow. The root Stripe Settings URI opens a PIN-protected screen and is separate from the blocked production Android Settings app.
